criteria.name: Correct identity and source-backed footprint
evidence: Purdue BuildingShapes feature FID 669 identifies 'Hockmeyer Hall of Structural Biology', building code HOCK; the saved page and plan snapshots also identify Hockmeyer Hall.
The reopened asset retains all 58 exterior-ring vertices from that official feature (exact_ring=True, maximum source-to-shell XY error 0.000035 m).

Independent OSM way 283274991 comparison yields IoU 96.28%, symmetric difference 3.72% and boundary Hausdorff 3.603 m. Boundary-to-segment distance fixes the earlier vertex-to-vertex sampling mismatch; Purdue remains the selected primary outline.

The apparent GIS area disagreement is explained by the saved native EPSG:3857 layer metadata and the expected Web Mercator area scale at Purdue latitude; the model follows the feature ring, not the distorted Shape__Area value.

criteria.name: Position, orientation, and scale/dimensions
evidence: Reopen comparison verifies the full 58-vertex source shell at 0.000035 m maximum XY error in the repository campus coordinate frame.
The documented project lon/lat-to-local-meter transform is applied to the authoritative Purdue geometry; OSM independently overlaps the outline by 96.28% of the union area.

Footprint alignment and its scale/orientation are strongly evidenced. A survey control network or published dimensioned plan was not found, so this does not establish survey accuracy; residual GIS/OSM boundary Hausdorff is 3.603 m.
criteria.deduction: Small deduction because the coordinate fit is source-precise but not tied to independent survey control or dimensioned architectural plans.

criteria.name: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
evidence: Purdue Biological Sciences (2010) describes the building as three-story; the current Purdue emergency plan independently supports three occupied floors and also mentions a penthouse and basement.
The asset models three floors, while 11.4 m is explicitly an estimate based on a 3 x 3.8 m floor-to-floor scaffold, not a measurement. GIS vertical fields are undocumented and correctly unused.
The asset has a flat cap. No evidence supports a measured roof silhouette or penthouse size/location; the known penthouse is omitted as a separate block rather than guessed.
criteria.deduction: Quantitative height, exact floor heights, detailed roof form, and penthouse geometry remain unverified or estimated.

criteria.name: Facade, entrances, and distinctive architecture
evidence: The official 2009 Purdue photo visibly supports red brick, large pale upper opaque panels, and blue-green multi-story glazing around the courtyard/arrival frontage.
The oblique and courtyard renders show these material zones, schematic curtainwall, brick windows and three-level rhythm; the roof-plan render exposes the GIS-derived re-entrant footprint.

The photo and landscape-architecture views are not registered to the GIS ring. Exact facade-edge correspondence, bay rhythm, and doorway location are therefore unverified; no precise entrance is fabricated in the model.
criteria.deduction: Major facade materials and glazing are supported, but their compass registration, exact bay layout, and entrance location are not verified.

criteria.name: Modular export, portability, and complete evidence
evidence: Asset file exists (True); expected collection 'Asset_massing_hockmeyer_hall_of_structural_biology_hock_4d524ab' reopens with 6 objects, including the main shell and facade components.
Direct reopen with Blender 4.5.15 LTS confirms the expected collection, 58 lower/upper shell vertices and no unpacked external dependencies ([]).
All three review renders are present and substantial (True); independent GIS, OSM, layer metadata, official photo and Purdue-plan source snapshots are present (True).

The expected scene ID does not match the Blender 4.5 actual scene ID ('Building_massing_hockmeyer_hall_of_structural_biology_hock_4d52' vs 'Building_massing_hockmeyer_hall_of_structural_biology_hock_4d524ab'); the full expected value is preserved in a custom property. This is recorded as a compatibility failure, not a pass.
criteria.deduction: The library collection and portable asset pass, but the expected scene-name contract fails on the available Blender 4.5 reopen path.

findings: The official Purdue 58-vertex shell is an exceptionally close source match; current OSM polygon-to-boundary metrics broadly corroborate it and replace the misleading earlier 16.27 m vertex-to-vertex comparison.
Three occupied floors are source-backed. The 11.4 m height is estimated; penthouse existence is documented, but its shape and location are not evidenced, and detailed roof form remains unresolved.
Facade palette and courtyard glazing match official imagery at a schematic level; facade registration and exact entrance placement remain unknown.

Expected collection reopens and has no external dependencies. Blender 4.5 truncates the expected long scene name; the full value is retained as a custom property but the scene-name contract itself remains failed.
